preferred_candidate_not_proven_safe.generated_c_signature: void Cysharp_Threading_Tasks_UniTask__Post(System_Action_o* action, int32_t timing, const MethodInfo* method)
preferred_candidate_not_proven_safe.reason: It is a named one-shot main-player-loop dispatch surface.
exact_build_native_flow: UniTask.Post moves the timing value to ECX, the Action pointer to RDX, clears the hidden MethodInfo slot in R8, and tail-jumps to PlayerLoopHelper.AddContinuation.

PlayerLoopHelper.AddContinuation resolves PlayerLoopHelper static fields, bounds-checks the timing index against the managed yielders array, selects the indexed ContinuationQueue, and tail-jumps to ContinuationQueue.Enqueue.

ContinuationQueue.Enqueue uses its SpinLock and stores the managed Action into actionList when idle or waitingList while RunCore is dequeuing; the managed array store applies the IL2CPP write barrier.

ContinuationQueue.RunCore invokes every Action through the delegate invoke pointer, clears consumed array entries, and swaps in the waiting list for a later pass instead of recursively invoking actions enqueued during the current pass.
A managed exception escaping one callback is caught, sent to UnityEngine.Debug.LogException, and the queue continues to the next callback.

delegate_requirements: A valid managed System.Action must be allocated using the exact current IL2CPP type and constructor contract.
The delegate target and trampoline must be valid, GC-rooted until invocation, exception-contained, and guaranteed to execute once.
The invoking thread must be attached to IL2CPP and all class/MethodInfo initialization requirements must be satisfied.
Lifecycle and leader gates must be rechecked inside the scheduled callback, not only before queueing.

alternative_candidate.limitations: This is a recurring registration, not a one-shot queue. It requires a live MonoBehaviour, an OnUpdate(float) delegate with the correct ABI, stable rooting, registration ownership, and guaranteed DelUpdate cleanup after success, cancellation, exception, scene transition, and shutdown.

other_rejected_candidates.status: engine-owned one-shot queue but not an external bridge
other_rejected_candidates.limitations: It still requires attached in-process execution plus a valid managed SendOrPostCallback and state object. It has no per-item removal API, so cancellation remains a callback-time check with the same race and lifetime problems.

other_rejected_candidates.status: component-owned one-shot list but not a general bridge
other_rejected_candidates.limitations: It requires discovery and lifetime ownership of a live Browser MonoBehaviour and appends the same managed Action shape to that component's thingsToDo list. It provides no external IPC, cancellation token, or scene-independent owner and is less suitable than the process-wide UniTask queue.

external_process_boundary.meaning: These exports make an in-process managed bridge mechanically conceivable but do not provide an IPC boundary. An external rLogs process cannot call them or supply a callback without executing code inside the game process.

scheduler_design_constraints.conclusion: The exact-build one-shot queue and its managed-array rooting semantics are statically proven, but no sanctioned external bridge, attached execution context, delegate/trampoline construction contract, race-free cancellation protocol, or lifecycle-safe callback ownership is proven. The scheduler remains a design candidate, not an activation contract.

required_fail_closed_gates.source_evidence: The reviewed normal game UI checks dungeon stage and compares TeamInfo.baseInfo.leaderId with the current character id before exposing scene-mask marker skills. An internal route would bypass that UI and therefore must duplicate the gates independently.

required_success_evidence: a matching self inbound marker-add notification is passively observed with the same scene/session, skill, and XYZ
pacing_and_acknowledgement.sequencing_rule: Permit only one marker in flight. Do not advance until both success signals match; abort on timeout, mismatch, lifecycle change, leader loss, scene change, or replacement/clear ambiguity.
pacing_and_acknowledgement.pacing_limit: One six-marker trace does not prove a safe minimum interval. Update, replacement, clear, rejection, reconnect, and scene-transition captures remain required.

simple_memory_write: Writing PlayerEnt__Storage._value105 bypasses the component API, change tracking, and object validity checks.
The value can be overwritten by ZIndicatorMgr or later game updates.
It creates no skill action, fresh session/authentication state, server authority, or party-visible marker.
SetIndicatorPos itself is a game method and is not equivalent to changing three floats.
raw_packet_injection: World.UseSlot carries dynamic slot, skill UUID, begin time, session sequence, authenticated/encrypted attribute data, call id, frame sequence, position, and transport ordering state.
Replaying captured constants would be stale and would bypass current eligibility, cooldown, lifecycle, and authorization logic.
A transport acknowledgement is not semantic marker acceptance.
The proposed game-owned route exists specifically so the current client creates all freshness and authority fields through its normal path.

unresolved_risks: No supported in-process entry, IL2CPP thread attachment, delegate allocation/rooting, or one-shot main-player-loop execution mechanism is proven. Exact normal callsites show that null hidden MethodInfo arguments are valid for the candidate methods, so MethodInfo acquisition is not the blocker.
No proof establishes that SetIndicatorPos followed by FirePlaySkillByIndicator is atomic against normal input or ZIndicatorMgr updates.
The exact leader, scene-transition, input-blocked, cooldown, and marker-replacement state queries at the internal boundary are not resolved.
The semantic meaning and lifetime of FirePlaySkillByIndicator's boolean result are not runtime-validated.
The server rate limit and failure behavior are not characterized beyond one successful six-marker trace.
Marker update, replacement, clear, rejection, reconnect, and stale-object behavior remain uncaptured.
Seasonal builds require a complete hash, RVA, layout, call-graph, and behavior re-audit.
